descr.name: Human Ether-a-go-go-Related Gene (hERG) channel small molecule antagonists: fluorescence cell-based qHTS assay
description: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences [NCATS]
National Institutes of Environmental Health Sciences [NIEHS]

Mutations in the hERG channel cause Long QT (LQT) syndrome. LQT syndrome is a cardiac disorder which can cause ventricle arrhythmia and sudden death. Additionally, compounds which block the hERG channel can cause acquired LQT syndrome. Several FDA approved drugs have been removed from the market due to their hERG blocking activity. A cell-based hERG channel inhibition assay can be used to screen chemical compounds that inhibit hERG channel.  This assay measures hERG channel activity using thallium ions as surrogate ions to measure potassium into the cells.
protocol: hERG-U2OS cells were resuspended in culture medium and dispensed into 1536-well, black wall/clear-bottom plates at 1000cells/well/3uL using a Multidrop Combi dispenser (Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA). After plates were incubated at 37 C overnight, 3 uL of Loading Buffer provided by FluxOR II Potassium Ion Channel Assay kit (Thermo, Carlsbad, CA) was added to each well. The assay plates were then incubated at room temperature in the dark for 1h. Following incubation, 23 nL of compound dissolved in DMSO, positive control (astemizole), or DMSO only was transferred to the assay plate. After the assay plates were incubated at room temperature for 10 min, 1 uL of Stimulus Buffer provided by FluxOR II Potassium Ion Channel Assay kit was added into each well and fluorescence intensity (480nm excitation/540nm emission) was continuously measured for 2 min at 1 second intervals using a Functional Drug Screening System (FDSS) 7000EX kinetic plate reader (Hamamatsu, Japan).
comment: Although all reasonable efforts have been made to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the data, caution should be exercised when interpreting the results as artifacts are possible from nonspecific effects such as assay signal interference. The curve fitting and activity calls presented here are based on the NCATS analysis methods. Alternative analysis methods and interpretations of the data are available at EPA (http://actor.epa.gov) and NTP (http://tools.niehs.nih.gov/cebs3/ui/).

1. Compounds are first classified as having full titration curves, partial modulation, partial curve (weaker actives), single point activity (at highest concentration only), or inactive. See data field "Curve Description". For this assay, apparent inhibitors are ranked higher than compounds that showed apparent activation.

2. For all inactive compounds, PUBCHEM_ACTIVITY_SCORE is 0. For all active compounds, a score range was given for each curve class type given above.  Active compounds have PUBCHEM_ACTIVITY_SCORE between 40 and 100.  Inconclusive compounds have PUBCHEM_ACTIVITY_SCORE between 1 and 39.  Fit_LogAC50 was used for determining relative score and was scaled to each curve class' score range.

results.name: Curve_Description-Replicate_14
description: A description of dose-response curve quality. A complete curve has two observed asymptotes; a partial curve may not have attained its second asymptote at the highest concentration tested. High efficacy curves exhibit efficacy greater than 80% of control. Partial efficacies are statistically significant, but below 80% of control.
